ORCHESTRA DEVEL 8 - Sharpe.description:
What should I play?
- Play the 2 octave scale and arpeggio (violin G Major two octaves, bass = G two octaves, viola/cello=C two octaves)
How should I play it?
Evenly at a steady tempo.  Slowly is fine.  Aim for accuracy and intonation.
- You may play it memorized or use the music for this recording.
- Bowing - choose what you are most confident doing now:  - with a rhythm on each note
- separate bows (one note per bow), or
- slur 2 or 4 notes per bow with even and clear notes.
-
- Grading is based on (SEE RUBRIC)
Feel free to add comments or ask questions in the video.
ARPEGGIO: 1st 3rd and 5th note of the scale up and down. (see the sheet)
Be sure to tune your instrument and review the correct key signature and finger patterns for your scale before recording.
Have "Major" Fun, and be sure to ask questions if you have any!

PLTW - 8 - Wingate.title: Fizzy Pop
PLTW - 8 - Wingate.description:
Did you know that programing/coding is an integral part in manufacturing beverages? It's true!  In fact, when you understand how coding works you begin to notice how it is applied all around you.
For example, freshly brewed coffee from a vending machine is one such example. Each coffee machine selection has a prescribed recipe and order of steps to make that perfect cup of coffee. When you push the selection button for your drink, the signal goes to the computer board. The computer board then signals the machine to drop the cup size you selected. The auger motors in the product bins (coffee beans, creamer, sugar, etc.) turn a specific number of prescribed rotations thereby releasing the amounts in the recipe. When they work as intended, you get that great tasting cup of coffee. If product is missing from the bin or an auger motor is not turning correctly, it may impact the taste and consumer satisfaction. Therefore, vending machine attendants check their product bins and do quality control checks regularly.
When the desired cup of coffee is not being produced by the machine, this is when a technician gets involved. He checks for error codes, troubleshoots, and may even reprogram the machine before doing quality control checks. Programming and coding are inseparable to that perfect cup of coffee.
In the "Fizzy Pop" activity, I want you to research two beverages. Your goal is to understand what makes them similar as well as what makes them different. After understanding how those beverages are produced in terms of ingredients and process, you will be ready to create your own beverage. Remember, the idea is to make a beverage recipe with ingredients so specific that you could trust another classmate to make that exact same drink without your help. Be creative and have some fun with it! I look forward to seeing what you develop!
Turn in your assignment here:
